summary: Cypher, wearing Tank's operator headgear, stands over the crew's jacked-in bodies on the main deck and reveals he has betrayed them. He admits to Trinity that he gave Morpheus to the Agents, justifying it by saying Morpheus "lied to us" and "tricked us," and that he prefers the Matrix, where he can be "fat and rich" and remember nothing. When Trinity insists "The Matrix isn't real," Cypher argues it "can be more real than this world," noting that here he only has to "pull a plug" whereas in the Matrix "you have to watch a man die." He then murders the helpless crew one by one: he yanks Apoc's neck cable, killing him; slides his hand to Switch's plug and kills her despite Trinity's pleas; and moves to Neo, taunting that if Neo is the One a "miracle" must stop him. Pressed for a yes-or-no on whether she believed Morpheus, Trinity whispers "yes" to Neo. Cypher cries "No!" as Tank, charred and bloody, suddenly levels a gun and fires a "CRACKLING BOLT of LIGHTNING" that knocks Cypher flying.

what_changes.before: Trinity realizes Cypher is behind the crew's deaths but does not yet know the full extent of his betrayal of Morpheus.
what_changes.after: She understands Cypher sold Morpheus to the Agents, declaring "My God. Morpheus. You gave them Morpheus."
what_changes.evidence: TRINITY My God. Morpheus. You gave them Morpheus.

what_changes.before: Cypher presents himself as a weary crew member, but is revealed to have chosen the Machines over Nebuchadnezzar.
what_changes.after: He openly declares his defection: "If I have to choose between that and the Matrix, I choose the Matrix," and that the Agents "promised to take me back."
what_changes.evidence: CYPHER If I have to choose between that and the Matrix, I choose the Matrix.

what_changes.before: Apoc is a living, confused crewman who reacts to Trinity's accusation.
what_changes.after: Cypher twists and yanks his neck cable and he "falls dead."
what_changes.evidence: He grabs hold of the cable in Apoc's neck, twists it and yanks it out.

what_changes.before: Switch is alive, begging "Not like this. Not like this."
what_changes.after: She is murdered, her body "severed from her mind."
what_changes.evidence: She suddenly feels her body severed from her mind as she is murdered.

what_changes.before: Neo lies jacked-in and helpless, with Cypher about to pull his plug.
what_changes.after: Tank appears and stops Cypher before he can kill Neo, firing a bolt that knocks Cypher back.
what_changes.evidence: He FIRES a CRACKLING BOLT of LIGHTNING that knocks Cypher flying backwards.

what_changes.before: Tank was reported to have "had an accident" and was presumed dead.
what_changes.after: He is revealed alive, "Charred and bloody," and levels a gun at Cypher.
what_changes.evidence: Charred and bloody, Tank levels the gun.

what_changes.before: Cypher demands she answer whether she believed Morpheus's claim about Neo.
what_changes.after: She confirms her belief, whispering "yes" as she looks at Neo.
what_changes.evidence: Trinity stares at Neo as a single word falls soundlessly from her lips.

event_hint.one_line: Cypher murders the jacked-in crew to hand them over to the Machines, but is stopped at the last moment by the surviving Tank.

objects_that_matter: the crew's neck plugs and cables
Trinity's body hanging in coma-like stillness
uncertain: Whether Morpheus is physically present on the deck or only being discussed.
Whether Neo is conscious and aware during Cypher's taunting.

minds.wants: To complete the betrayal by killing every jacked-in crew member, erasing the last witnesses to his deal with the Machines.
minds.feels: A cold, exhausted resentment that has curdled into entitlement; he has reframed murder as a transaction ("just the messenger") so he never has to feel it as killing.
minds.shows: A languid, almost tender performance — nuzzling Trinity, calling her beautiful, joking ("Welcome to the real world, eh baby?") — the ease of a man who believes he has already won.
minds.basis: He uses Tank's headgear, speaks of being 'tired' of the ship and Morpheus, and treats each plug-pull as a casual chore, laughing at the 'American dream' while Apoc and Switch die.

believes_about.belief: That Morpheus tricked the crew into a life of suffering and deserves to be broken by the Agents.
believes_about.wrong_because: He recasts Morpheus's gift of freedom as a con, because he cannot bear the truth that he chose to reject that freedom himself.

believes_about.belief: That Neo is a helpless body he can kill at will, and that no 'miracle' will intervene.
believes_about.wrong_because: He is about to learn Neo is the One — his taunt ('some kind of miracle to stop me') is the exact threshold his survival fails to cross.

believes_about.belief: That Tank is dead ('had an accident'), leaving no one to stop him.
believes_about.wrong_because: Tank is alive, charred and armed, and is the instrument that ends Cypher.

believes_about.belief: That they will honor their promise to reinsert his body and let him forget.
believes_about.wrong_because: They are machines that use and discard; the 'deal' is a lie he tells himself to make betrayal palatable.

minds.wants: To keep Neo alive by holding Cypher in the argument long enough for something — anything — to break his certainty.
minds.feels: Terror and grief, compounded by the horror of realizing Cypher sold Morpheus, not merely killed the others; she is trapped in a body that cannot fight back.
minds.shows: Defiance in words ('The Matrix isn't real!', 'You're out, you can't go back') but pleading in extremis ('Oh no, please don't'), finally compressing everything into a silent 'yes'.
minds.basis: She argues the nature of reality to stall him, begs for Switch, and when forced to a yes-or-no, looks into Neo's eyes and whispers 'yes' — an act of faith, not just an answer.

believes_about.belief: That he is a murderer and traitor beyond reach.
believes_about.wrong_because: Not wrong in substance — but she underestimates how completely he has convinced himself, which is why argument cannot move him.

believes_about.belief: That he may truly be the One, and that her affirmation might summon the miracle Cypher demands.
believes_about.wrong_because: Uncertain even to her; the 'yes' is faith willed against fear, not confirmed knowledge.

minds.wants: To survive — but he can do nothing; his entire agency is reduced to being the object of another's belief.
minds.feels: Helplessness and fear, aware he is next, forced into the most passive test imaginable: whether someone else's faith can save him.
minds.shows: Nothing observable — he lies jacked-in and silent; the scene registers him only through Trinity's gaze and Cypher's taunt.
minds.basis: Cypher stands over him, says 'he knows he is next,' and demands a miracle; Trinity turns to him with 'eyes wide with fear.'

believes_about.belief: That he cannot stop what is happening to him.
believes_about.wrong_because: This is the last moment he will ever be this powerless; the miracle Cypher mocks is what his arc is about to become.

minds.wants: To stop Cypher before Neo's plug is pulled — to avenge Dozer and the others in the same motion.
minds.feels: Pain and fury from his own near-death, now focused into a single lethal purpose.
minds.shows: Charred and bloody, he levels the gun and fires without hesitation — action, not speech, except to mark Cypher as 'going to burn.'
minds.basis: He was presumed dead ('had an accident' in sc-140), survives wounded, and appears at the exact instant Cypher's certainty peaks ('No!' / 'I don't believe it!').

believes_about.belief: That Cypher is a traitor who must be destroyed, with no room for parley.
believes_about.wrong_because: Not wrong — this is one belief in the scene that is simply correct.

minds.wants: To understand what is happening — his last conscious reach is toward Trinity ('Trinity?').
minds.feels: Confusion tipping into animal terror as his body is 'severed from his mind.'
minds.shows: A scream caught in his throat, hands 'reaching for nothing,' then death.
minds.basis: His single line 'What?!' and 'Trinity?' and the described death — 'go blind for an instant... reaching for nothing, and then falls dead.'

minds.wants: Dignity in dying — 'Not like this' — a plea against the helplessness of her murder.
minds.feels: Dread and a specific horror at being killed while utterly defenseless.
minds.shows: A repeated plea ('Not like this. Not like this.') as Trinity is forced to witness.
minds.basis: Her dialogue and the sensation of her 'body severed from her mind as she is murdered.'

connects_back: Cypher's 'He had an accident' lie in sc-140 masks that Tank survived, which is the whole mechanism of this scene's reversal.
The crew already jacked into the Matrix (to reach Morpheus, per ev-024) is why they lie helpless and why Cypher can murder them at the plugs.
Dozer's death (sc-139) and Tank's injury are the immediate cause of Tank's charred, vengeful entrance here.
Cypher's earlier resentment of Morpheus and the 'red pill' (established across the film) is what he now weaponizes as justification.
sets_up: The crew is reduced to the survivors who will mount Morpheus's rescue (ev-026), with Tank restored as operator.
Trinity's affirmed faith in Neo as the One becomes the emotional stake carried into the rescue and the subway (ev-028, ev-030).
Cypher's death closes the internal threat, leaving only the Machines as the crew's opposition going forward.
Tank's survival and lethal competence re-establish the ship's ability to operate for the coming raid (ev-025–027).
dramatic_function: This is the story's betrayal-climax and its faith-test: it strips the crew to nothing, forcing Trinity to choose belief over proof, and stages Cypher's murder as the dark mirror of the film's central question — whether the Matrix is real — right before the 'miracle' he mocks is about to answer.
